history.summary: Built in 1912 by Billava community leader and businessman Adhyaksha HoigeBazar Koragappa under the spiritual guidance of Sree Narayana Guru, the Kerala philosopher and social reformer. Koragappa, hurt that members of his Billava community were denied entry into Mangalore's temples, resolved to build a temple open to all; Narayana Guru selected the site at Kudroli (between Mulihithilu and Kudroli) and brought the Shivalinga himself, consecrating it in February 1912 as 'Gokarnanatha'. The temple is accepted as 'Aadi' by the Billava community. Its tall gopuram is decorated with murals depicting Hindu epics and legends. The present grand complex dates to a 1991 renovation. Since 1991 it has been the centre of the grand Mangalore Dasara Navaratri celebrations, featuring the 'Gangavatharana' display (four 13-ft Shiva idols with 100-ft water jets).

name: Kudroli Gokarnanatheshwara Temple
town_description: Mangaluru (formerly Mangalore) is a major port city on the Arabian Sea coast of Karnataka, the administrative headquarters of Dakshina Kannada district and the heart of Tulu-speaking Tulunadu. Known for its beaches, banking and education institutions, and diverse cuisine, it is also a temple city whose ancient shrines anchor the region's religious life.
